findings.message: Dropping the `now.Sub(FinishedAt) < evictOOMThreshold` recency guard makes `quickOOM` permanently true for any container whose `LastTerminationState` records a fast OOM, no matter how long ago it happened. Since `quickOOM` short-circuits the `!updatePriority.OutsideRecommendedRange && !quickOOM` block, such a pod bypasses PodLifetimeUpdateThreshold and MinChangePriority on every pass and is repeatedly admitted for update whenever ResourceDiff != 0.

The only test asserting that a stale quick OOM does not force an update is deleted, so the behavior change is untested. The surviving TestDontUpdatePodWithOOMAfterLongRun covers only the long-runtime branch, which the remaining `FinishedAt.Sub(StartedAt) < evictOOMThreshold` term still handles.

findings.message: `lastCheckpointGC` is now stamped before GC runs, and GC can no longer report failure, so a failed or context-cancelled garbage collection is recorded as a success and will not be retried for a full `checkpointsGCInterval` (10m by default).

This is exactly the case the deleted `TestMaintainCheckpointsGCUsesIndependentTimeout` covered.

verdicts.reason: The revert is mechanically complete and self-consistent: the `GarbageCollectCheckpoints` signature change from `error` to no return matches both the interface and the only production caller, the `CheckpointsGCTimeout` field is removed from the struct, defaults, flag registration, validation, `RecommenderFactory`, and `recommender_controller.go` together, the now-unused `errors` import is dropped while `fmt` stays (still used by other error paths in cluster_feeder.go), the one test call site is updated, and the generated flags doc row is removed. No broken name, missing caller update, or inverted condition found. What remains is the behavioural regression the revert restores: `lastCheckpointGC` is stamped before GC executes and GC can no longer signal failure, so an error — including a context already exhausted by `StoreCheckpoints` under the shared `checkpointsWriteTimeout` deadline in `RunOnce` — is logged and then treated as a completed GC, deferring the next attempt by a full GC interval. That is precisely what the deleted `TestMaintainCheckpointsGCUsesIndependentTimeout` asserted against, so if the revert is intentional it is acceptable; if only the flag was meant to go away, keep the error return and stamp `lastCheckpointGC` only on success.

findings.message: Reverting to strings.Split(id[7:], "/")[1] reintroduces issue #8305: a placeholder name containing '/' (e.g. aws:///us-east-1a/i-placeholder-some/arbitrary/cluster/local) passes validation via the placeholder alternative but Name is truncated to "i-placeholder-some", so CA cannot associate the placeholder with its ASG and scaling stalls after MaxNodeStartupTime.

locations.message: Both regression cases are deleted in the same commit as the behaviour change, so the '/'-in-placeholder-name case (#8305) and the 'i-foo-i-placeholder-bar' substring case are no longer covered and the truncation regression passes silently.

verdicts.reason: The change reverts the #8305 fix in the AWS provider-ID parser: the regex stops acting as the extractor and the name is again derived with strings.Split(id[7:], \"/\")[1], which cannot represent a placeholder name containing '/', so such names are truncated and CA can no longer match the placeholder to its ASG (violation of the 'never split provider IDs on /' note). The new placeholder alternative also lost its leading '^' anchor, letting prefixed garbage validate and yielding a wrong name from the misaligned id[7:] slice. The two regression tests that pinned this behaviour were deleted in the same commit, so the regression is untested. Separately, the note about the three capture groups and the len(matches)==4 guard no longer matches the code and needs rewriting.

findings.message: Placeholder instance names containing '/' are truncated at the first slash. The regex still matches such IDs via the placeholder alternative ('%s.*$'), but the name is taken as strings.Split(id[7:], "/")[1], so 'aws:///us-east-1a/i-placeholder-some/arbitrary/cluster/local' yields Name="i-placeholder-some" instead of the full name. This reintroduces kubernetes/autoscaler#8305, whose regression test is deleted in the same change.

The placeholder alternative of the regex lost its '^' anchor, so IDs with arbitrary leading characters (e.g. "xxaws:///us-east-1a/i-placeholder-x") now pass validation. Since extraction uses the hardcoded offset id[7:] (len("aws:///")), the split is misaligned and Name becomes the zone or an empty string rather than the instance name. Every branch of the previous regex was '^'-anchored.

Both regression tests removed here are the ones that would catch the truncation defect: the multi-slash placeholder case and the ordinary name containing the placeholder prefix as a substring. After their removal the suite passes despite the wrong Name for slash-bearing placeholder IDs.

verdicts.reason: The change reverts capture-group-based name extraction in AwsRefFromProviderId to a fixed-offset strings.Split, and removes the two regression tests that pinned that behaviour. Two real defects: (1) placeholder instance names containing "/" are now truncated at the first slash (splitted[1]), reintroducing kubernetes/autoscaler#8305, since the regex still accepts them via the unanchored placeholder alternative; (2) that placeholder alternative lost its leading "^" anchor, so IDs with leading junk validate while id[7:] misaligns, producing the zone or an empty string as Name. Validation and extraction are no longer derived from the same match, and the deleted tests mean nothing fails on either defect.

findings.message: This reverts the ResizeStatusError mapping to utils.InPlaceInfeasible, which writes the current recommendation into the in-memory infeasibleAttempts cache. That cache is only cleared when a later recommendation is *lower* (see the RecommendationHasLowerResource guard earlier in this same function), so a transient kubelet resize error (e.g. a missing memory usage reading) permanently blocks higher recommendations for the pod until the Updater restarts. Per the recorded fix pattern, only genuinely permanent capacity failures (utils.ResizeStatusInfeasible) may return InPlaceInfeasible; recoverable/unknown states must return InPlaceDeferred.

Worth wording as "lower recommendation" to match the code.

verdicts.reason:
The change flips the `utils.ResizeStatusError` branch of `CanInPlaceUpdate` from `InPlaceDeferred` back to `InPlaceInfeasible`, and consistently updates the three companion locations (interface doc comment, the features.md resize-status row, and the `TestInPlaceModeResizeStatuses` case name/expectation) — so the "keep the mapping in sync" convention is respected mechanically.

However, the substance of the mapping directly contradicts the recorded invariant that only permanent capacity failures may return `InPlaceInfeasible`. The code shown still supports that note: the same function caches `InPlaceInfeasible` recommendations and only reconsiders them via `!resourcehelpers.RecommendationHasLowerResource(lastAttempt, recommendation)`, i.e. only when a later recommendation is lower. A transient kubelet resize error therefore silently blocks all higher recommendations for that pod until the Updater process restarts — exactly the symptom the note documents. This is the main finding (error).

Secondary, minor: both the new features.md row and the doc comment say the retry happens "when the recommendation changes", while the implementation requires a strictly *lower* recommendation. No notes are contradicted by the code, so nothing is marked outdated.

The change flips the `utils.ResizeStatusError` branch of `CanInPlaceUpdate` from `InPlaceDeferred` to `InPlaceInfeasible`, and updates the interface doc comment, the `features.md` status table, and the corresponding table-driven test expectation. All four edits point the same way, the return value is an existing member of `utils.InPlaceDecision` already handled by the neighbouring `ResizeStatusInfeasible` branch, and the function signature/contract is unchanged so no callers need updating. `klog.V(4).ErrorS` is a valid klog API. findings.message: Reverting the OOM staleness check to use WindowEnd reintroduces kubernetes/autoscaler#8548: WindowEnd is the end of the current aggregation interval and is advanced by usage samples, so it can be up to a full interval (24h default) ahead of the latest real sample. A fresh OOM that landed just before an interval boundary is then Before(WindowEnd-interval) and is wrongly discarded, losing the OOM bump-up.

The regression test for the boundary case is deleted along with the fix, so nothing remains that distinguishes the WindowEnd cutoff from the lastMemorySampleStart cutoff; TestRecordOOMInNewWindow passes under either, leaving the reintroduced bug uncovered.

verdicts.reason: The change reverts the OOM staleness check in RecordOOM from a lastMemorySampleStart-based cutoff back to a WindowEnd-based one and deletes the accompanying regression test. Since WindowEnd is the end of the current aggregation interval and can sit up to a full interval ahead of the newest real sample, this reintroduces kubernetes/autoscaler#8548: a wall-clock-fresh OOM arriving just before an interval boundary is discarded as 'too old' and its bump-up is lost. The removed test was the only coverage distinguishing the two cutoffs. The dropped IsZero guard is benign (zero WindowEnd yields a cutoff in year 1) but leaves the precondition implicit.

findings.message: RecordOOM's "too old" check is reverted to use WindowEnd as the reference point. WindowEnd is the end of the current memory aggregation interval and is pushed a whole interval forward by addMemorySample when a sample crosses a boundary, so it can lead the newest real sample by up to one full interval (24h default). A fresh OOM that landed just before a boundary is then classified as older than one interval and silently discarded - the regression described in kubernetes/autoscaler#8548. Anchor the comparison to container.lastMemorySampleStart (guarded with !IsZero()) instead.

verdicts.reason: The change reverts the #8548 fix in ContainerState.RecordOOM, restoring the staleness comparison against WindowEnd (an aggregation-interval boundary that can lead the newest real sample by a full interval) instead of lastMemorySampleStart, and deletes the regression test that covered it. This directly contradicts two cached rules whose claims the surrounding code still supports (addMemorySample still advances WindowEnd by whole intervals; lastMemorySampleStart still exists), so fresh OOMs landing just before a boundary will again be discarded as \"too old\" and no memory bump-up will happen. The remaining notes (recommender flags, per-step context timeouts, updater lastState recency, desired replica counts) are unrelated to this diff, and no note was found to be outdated.

findings.message: Resource name is interpolated into the JSON Pointer without escaping, so extended resources like `nvidia.com/gpu` yield the invalid path `/spec/containers/2/resources/limits/nvidia.com/gpu`. The API server rejects the patch and, with the default FailurePolicy: Ignore, the pod is admitted unmutated — VPA resource policies are silently bypassed. Route the segment through an escape helper (`~` -> `~0` first, then `/` -> `~1`).

locations.message: The entire test file is deleted, removing the only coverage that pinned patch-path escaping (cases 'Extended resource with slash', 'Extended resource with tilde and slash', and the annotation tilde cases). Nothing now guards against the regression reintroduced in util.go.

Annotation name escaping reverted to a single hand-rolled ReplaceAll for `/` only; a `~` in the annotation key is left unescaped and produces an invalid JSON Pointer. The note's fix pattern requires `~` -> `~0` before `/` -> `~1` and explicitly warns against a single ReplaceAll for `/` only.

verdicts.reason: The change reverts the RFC 6901 escaping of user/API-supplied path segments in the VPA admission controller's patch builders and deletes the test file that pinned the behaviour. `GetAddResourceRequirementValuePatch` now interpolates the raw `corev1.ResourceName` into the JSON Pointer, so extended resources such as `nvidia.com/gpu` again produce an invalid path and the webhook patch is rejected (the exact symptom the note `vpa-admission-patch-paths-must-escape-and-per-rfc-6901` describes). The annotation builders fall back to the hand-rolled single `ReplaceAll(..., "/", "~1")` the same note explicitly forbids, leaving `~` unescaped. All other notes are unrelated to this change; none are contradicted by the code.

findings.message: Resource names are no longer escaped: an extended resource like `nvidia.com/gpu` yields `/spec/containers/2/resources/limits/nvidia.com/gpu`, which JSON Patch reads as a nested object `nvidia.com` with key `gpu` instead of the single key `nvidia.com~1gpu`. Patches for any vendor/extended resource now target the wrong location.

findings.message: The `~` -> `~0` escaping step is dropped. Per RFC 6901 a literal `~` must be escaped; and replacing `/` with `~1` without first escaping `~` is ambiguous, so an annotation named `a~1b` now produces the same path as `a/b`.
findings.evidence:
-		Path:  fmt.Sprintf("/metadata/annotations/%s", escapeJSONPatchPath(annotationName)),
+		Path:  fmt.Sprintf("/metadata/annotations/%s", strings.ReplaceAll(annotationName, "/", "~1")),

verdicts.reason: The change inlines a partial version of the removed `escapeJSONPatchPath` helper and drops escaping entirely for resource names. Result: `~` is no longer escaped to `~0` in annotation paths (invalid/ambiguous RFC 6901 pointers), and extended resource names containing `/` (e.g. `nvidia.com/gpu`) now produce paths with a raw slash that JSON Patch interprets as a nested path, so the patch targets the wrong location. The deleted util_test.go asserted precisely these behaviors, so the regressions are now unguarded.
